candidate.title: X-ChIP
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina X-ChIP schematic, identified as high-resolution X-ChIP-seq by the matching collection heading and caption: in vivo crosslinking, cell lysis, MNase digestion, sonication to soluble chromatin, and antibody enrichment with DNA extraction. One material route with no alternative or pooled branches is depicted. X-ChIP and X-ChIP-seq denote the enrichment workflow and its sequencing use here; complete implementations across those names are not asserted identical. The left target inset is descriptive, and the final DNA is a substrate for an unpictured downstream sequencing library.

states.label: Cells with in vivo chromatin-associated proteins
features: Intact starting cells are drawn as a green cell with a nucleus.

The far-left nucleosome/DNA illustration is a descriptive target inset labeled "High resolution of mapping of in vivo chromatin associated proteins (X-ChIP)"; it has no transfer arrow into the cell workflow.

states.label: DNA extracted from immunoprecipitated chromatin
features: DNA is the depicted endpoint, drawn as two parallel blue lines labeled "DNA"; adapters, barcodes, and specific end groups are not depicted.
DNA enrichment reflects association with the antibody-selected chromatin protein or epitope, rather than sequencing the protein itself.
For the supported high-resolution sequencing use, DNA sequence locates associated genomic regions and paired-end fragment boundaries and lengths can report protected footprints.
Recovered DNA can include indirect crosslinked complexes; antibody enrichment does not establish that every fragment is a direct binding footprint.
The catalogue reports short-fragment enrichment and sequencing-library preparation downstream; these are an unpictured interface, not additional drawn operations.

operations.label: Crosslink cells in vivo
operations.description: Fix chromatin associations inside cells, producing crosslinked cells before their contents are released.
operations.mechanism: Formaldehyde crosslinking stabilizes chromatin-associated protein and nucleic-acid associations.
operations.information_effect: Preserves in vivo associations for subsequent enrichment; fixation can also preserve indirect protein-mediated associations. Long fixation can retain transient as well as stable interactions, so enrichment is not a residence-time measurement.

operations.label: Lyse cells
operations.description: Disrupt the crosslinked cells to make their chromatin accessible outside the intact cell; the output is the material labeled "Cross-linked chromatin".
operations.information_effect: Releases the chromatin material while retaining the fixation history; no selection of a particular chromatin protein is depicted at this step.

evidence.locator: Left-middle: second cell to "Cross-linked chromatin", arrow captioned "Lyse cells"

operations.label: MNase digestion
operations.description: Digest DNA in the crosslinked chromatin, leaving protein-protected DNA fragments before solubilization.
operations.mechanism: Micrococcal nuclease provides endo- and exonuclease activity; the primary paper identifies unprotected DNA as the digested substrate.
operations.information_effect: Fragment boundaries can approach protected regions, carrying footprint information on the surviving DNA; the drawing specifies no end-group chemistry.

operations.label: Sonicate
operations.description: Sonicate the MNase-treated crosslinked chromatin to yield the separated chromatin complexes labeled "Soluble extract".
operations.mechanism: The catalogue identifies this as solubilization by brief sonication after MNase digestion.
operations.information_effect: Makes the digested protein-associated DNA available for immunoprecipitation. MNase is the principal footprint-generating fragmentation step in the cited high-resolution implementation.

operations.label: Immunoprecipitate and DNA extraction
operations.description: Use antibody recognition to enrich chromatin complexes from the soluble extract and recover their associated DNA. The shared diagram caption combines selection and DNA extraction without depicting an intermediate isolation state.
operations.mechanism: Antibody-directed chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by DNA recovery; the target protein or epitope is unspecified.
operations.information_effect: Target association is transferred into an enriched DNA population. Downstream sequencing libraries represent these recovered genomic fragments, and short protected fragments can support high-resolution localization; neither perfect specificity nor exclusively direct binding is established.
